results.name: Soda Cans
results.description:
A drink can (or beverage can) is a metal container designed to hold a fixed portion of liquid such as carbonated soft drinks, alcoholic drinks, fruit juices, teas, herbal teas, energy drinks, etc. Drink cans are made of aluminium (75% of worldwide production) or tin-plated steel (25% worldwide production). Worldwide production for all drink cans is approximately 370 billion cans per year worldwide.

results.name: Soda Cans 3D pack
results.description:
This is the Soda Cans 3D pack! 
This pack contains various models of a Soda Can to fit your need! Each type of soda can comes in two size: A regular size Soda Can and a smaller size Soda Can (both of which are modelled using real world dimensions)
Included in this pack is:

- Mid poly Soda Cans (which can be used for ads, product animations and close up shots)

- Lower poly Soda Cans (Which can be used for background models or low end PC's)

- Crushed Soda Cans [Rigged for Blender (comes with a lattice controller)]

- Baked Crushed Soda cans (For those not using Blender)
This comes in 3 height presets: Regular, medium and low

Each of these models are UV unwrapped and modelled with excellent quad meshes. This pack also includes a copy of these models with triangulated meshes for games and CAD softwares.

This soda can model was used for my SLOSH soda can project: https://www.behance.net/gallery/181147027/3D-Can-product-render-(2D-to-3D)

Rigged | High poly | Low poly | Controller | Baked | Quads | Triangular

results.name: Nuka Cola
results.description:
Following the last Fallout fan Art I did , I decided I wanted to make a more detailed version of everyone's favorite Soft drink.

![](https://cdna0.artstation.com/p/assets/images/images/002/832/312/large/oscar-velasco-nuka-cola-jpeg-01.jpg?1466226471)

![](https://cdna2.artstation.com/p/assets/images/images/002/832/314/large/oscar-velasco-nuka-cola-jpeg-02.jpg?1466226481)


You can watch  the model rendered here 
https://www.artstation.com/artwork/5Ygew

EDIT: I  did  a  re-upload,  I got rid of many  unnecessary polygons, like those condensation drops (they were polygonal) , and went for a more texture based solution to represent the condensation.

The Uv mapping  is not so good,  specially on the backside, you can see the seams of the textures, but yeah. I preffer it this way than the older version, which was to heavy  and made the navigation too slow. This one is more fluid.
Enjoy ;)

No copyright infringement intended
Just  Fan Art

results.name: Pepsi Can
results.description:
Pepsi was first introduced as "Brad's Drink"[2] in New Bern, North Carolina, United States, in 1893 by Caleb Bradham, who made it at his drugstore where the drink was sold. It was renamed Pepsi-Cola in 1898 after the root of the word "dyspepsia" and the kola nuts used in the recipe. The original recipe also included sugar and vanilla. Bradham sought to create a fountain drink that was appealing and would aid in digestion and boost energy.
